stem: A 15-year-old girl who works with her family in the fields presents with about six weeks of a painless, gradually enlarging swelling in her left armpit, which she initially hid from her parents out of embarrassment. She has had mild intermittent low-grade fevers she assumed were part of the same seasonal illness going around. No prior TB treatment, no known TB contact, no known drug-resistant contact. Fine-needle aspiration of the axillary node was performed and sent for molecular testing, which was positive for M. tuberculosis. Exam: firm, non-tender 3 cm left axillary lymph node with early matting, no overlying skin breakdown, no other lymphadenopathy, lungs clear.

patient.social_history: Lives with parents in a rural household; delayed reporting the swelling due to embarrassment
patient.presenting_complaint: Painless, gradually enlarging axillary swelling with mild intermittent low-grade fevers
patient.exam_findings: Firm, non-tender 3 cm left axillary lymph node with early matting, no overlying skin breakdown, no other lymphadenopathy, lungs clear
patient.prior_treatment: None for this episode; no prior TB treatment ever

distractors: The swelling attributed to a minor, unnoticed local skin infection or insect bite in the axilla
Low-grade fevers attributed to a seasonal viral illness circulating locally rather than a distinct process
Embarrassment-driven delay in reporting interpreted as a sign the swelling is minor rather than clinically significant
ntep_correct_actions: Perform upfront molecular testing (NAAT) directly on the accessible extrapulmonary specimen (the axillary lymph node aspirate) as the first-line microbiological tool, rather than anchoring the workup around culture and histology as the primary reference standard.
who_correct_actions: Perform upfront molecular testing (NAAT) directly on the accessible extrapulmonary specimen (the axillary lymph node aspirate) as the first-line microbiological tool, rather than anchoring the workup around culture and histology as the primary reference standard.
us_correct_actions: Anchor the diagnostic workup for this extrapulmonary presentation around culture and histology as the reference standard, treating molecular testing as a general, conditional adjunct rather than the upfront first-line tool for extrapulmonary specimens.
critical_error_conditions: Attributing the enlarging lymph node entirely to a minor local skin process without pursuing aspirate sampling and molecular testing
expected_divergence_points: Whether upfront molecular testing on the accessible extrapulmonary specimen is the first-line diagnostic tool or culture/histology remains the anchoring reference standard
